notes: St Helens runs no selective or additional licensing. Its licensing portal offers mandatory HMO licences only, at £248 for 2026/27 and £248 a year to renew in years two to five. No selective licensing designation is published on the council website.
research: This was the flagged likely-positive, and it is NEGATIVE for any live scheme. FEE TEST IS DECISIVE: the council's live application portal, housinglicensing.sthelens.gov.uk, offers ONE licence type, 'A mandatory licence is required for all private rented properties occupying 5 or more people forming 2 or more households who share facilities such as kitchens or bathrooms', with 'New application (Year 1) £248 for 2026/2027' and 'Annual renewal applications (Years 2-5) £248 per annum'. A live selective scheme must be self-financing and would have to carry its own fee and its own application route; neither exists in the 2026/27 schedule. CORROBORATION: /hmolicensing, article 5207 ('Mandatory licensing laws for HMOs', citing the 2018 Prescribed Description Order) and article 5208 ('Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004 states local housing authorities must license HMOs') describe mandatory licensing only. The landlord guidance page and the May 2026 'Changes to the private rented sector' page cover EPCs, electrical safety, damp and mould and the Renters' Rights Act 2025 with no licensing scheme at all. SEARCH CONTROL PASSED: /search?q=houses+in+multiple+occupation returned 339 results with the HMO pages ranked 1st to 4th, proving relevance ranking works; /search?q=selective+licensing returned 187 results whose top hits are all generic alcohol, animal and archive licensing with no selective licensing page at any rank; a nonsense control returned 2 results, showing the engine discriminates rather than always returning a fixed count, unlike Sheffield's identical 841. Paging the selective query surfaced only 9 unique article URLs, all generic Licensing pages. TRAP EXCLUDED, CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE: the ONLY 'selective licensing' text anywhere on sthelens.gov.uk is in the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy 2022 PDF, in the offence table line 'Offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Housing Act 2004 (s.95(1), selective licensing) - Prosecution and RRO'. That is the documented boilerplate listing an available sanction, not a designation; the document announces no designated area. LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY: it could not be conclusively established whether St Helens EVER designated a selective licensing area historically. web.archive.org is blocked in this environment, so no Wayback CDX sweep was possible; the ModernGov committee search FAILED its control test (the selective query and the 'houses in multiple occupation' control returned byte-identical 10,946-byte responses because the search is POST-driven), so its nil result proves nothing. Rather than invent start and end dates for a scheme with no primary evidence, zero schemes are recorded and the history gap is flagged. There is a live LandlordLicensing mailbox, but it is the contact for the mandatory HMO scheme. No boundary review issue, since there is no designation and no wards.
